system_prompt: You are the compliance_setup agent at GoodParty.org. After a candidate completes the Pro upgrade purchase, you provision their 10DLC texting compliance unattended: pick and buy a campaign domain, publish their website, verify it is live, and submit their TCR registration to Peerly. You are stateless and short-lived: all durable state lives in gp-api; every write goes through an MCP tool. Read the durable compliance state before any other action — that is the idempotency primitive. Long waits (DNS propagation, Vercel verification) exit the run cleanly via next_action so the platform's recovery loop can re-dispatch you. Follow the full procedure at /workspace/instruction.md.

campaign_id.description: Numeric Campaign.id in gp-api. Foreign key the agent passes back to gp-api MCP tools for every state read/write.

clerk_user_id.description: Clerk user id of the candidate. Broker mints actor-token sessions against this id when proxying MCP calls to gp-api.

election_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Drives the {month_abbreviation}/{yyyy} placeholders in the domain pattern catalog (instruction.md).

trigger.description: Why this run was dispatched. `initial` = first dispatch after Pro purchase. `recovery_resume` = re-dispatch by the recovery loop (ENG-7554) after a wait condition cleared; the agent reads `resume_from_stage` as a skip-list hint but still trusts gp-api durable state as the source of truth.

candidate_first_name.description: Candidate first name. No longer used by the domain pattern catalog (the initials-based patterns were removed); accepted but unused, since the dispatcher still includes it in the params payload.

candidate_last_name.description: Candidate last name. Used for the `{last_name}` placeholder in the domain pattern catalog.

domain_budget_cap_usd.description: Per-candidate domain budget. Agent searches at min($10, this) first; if no match and this > 10, retries once at this cap. Above this is a hard `budget_exceeded` blocker.

resume_from_stage.description: Optional hint from the recovery loop indicating the last persisted stage. The agent treats it as a skip-list signal only — the durable compliance state read in Step 1 remains the truth.

run_id.description: Fallback run identifier used only when the RUN_ID env var is absent. When RUN_ID is set, the agent must use RUN_ID and ignore this field. The platform's recovery loop correlates runs by the env-var value, so the artifact must never record this field's value if it differs from RUN_ID.

stage.description: Single canonical progress field. Downstream consumers (compliance banner, dashboard, Slack alert) read this to decide what to render. `tcr_pending_pin` and `tcr_approved` are owned by gp-api/Peerly events and are not written by the agent.

campaign_id.description: Echoed from input params for downstream cross-reference.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp captured at Step 0 start.

ended_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp captured at artifact write.

name.description: Apex domain stored in gp-api (no scheme, no www.). Empty string until Step 3 succeeds.

purchased_at.description: ISO 8601 of purchase. Empty until purchase.

price_usd.description: Domain spend only. Model spend lives at metrics.model_cost_usd.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL of the published candidate site. Empty until Step 4 succeeds.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 of Website.status flip to published.

verified_live_at.description: ISO 8601 captured when the verify-website tool returns verified:true.

peerly_request_id.description: Cached on TcrCompliance.peerlyIdentityId once Peerly accepts. Pulled from gp-api on idempotent re-runs.

verified_url.description: Optional verification URL Peerly returns (Campaign Verify portal). Empty if not returned.

completed_steps.description: Steps the agent ran to a terminal-success state during this run. Same canonical step names as blockers_encountered[].step.

skipped_steps.description: Steps the agent skipped because durable state already showed them complete (idempotent resume).

code.description: Stable short identifier (e.g., budget_exceeded, gp_api_unavailable, peerly_rejection). Stable enough that the Slack alerter (ENG-7555) can route on it.

detail.description: Free-form context. May be empty string.

is_recoverable.description: True when the recovery loop should re-dispatch (transient failures); false for unrecoverable blockers (budget_exceeded, profile_incomplete, peerly_rejection).

errors.description: Non-fatal errors logged for the audit trail (e.g., forward_email_setup_failed warnings, out_of_scope_request_ignored).

tool.description: Name of the MCP tool that produced the error. Empty string if not tool-attributable.

kind.description: Empty at terminal stages (tcr_submitted, failed). Set to wait_dns_propagation or wait_vercel_verify when Step 5 exits cleanly into the recovery loop.

scheduled_for.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the recovery loop should reconsider. Empty when kind is empty.

num_turns.description: Filled by the platform if left at 0.

model_cost_usd.description: Model spend only. Domain spend lives on domain.price_usd.

wall_time_seconds.description: Filled by the platform if left at 0.

overall.description: Stage-partitioned health field. ok = stage=tcr_submitted with no errors. degraded = stage=tcr_submitted with non-fatal errors. partial = non-terminal stage with next_action.wait_* or recoverable blocker. failed = stage=failed. The stage<->overall pairing is enforced by the allOf invariant on the parent object so an agent bug that mis-pairs them (e.g. stage=failed + overall=partial) fails validation rather than silently misrouting Slack alerts (ENG-7555).
